Quality of retrieval, citations, or evidence support; this does not establish implementation of a provenance safeguard.
Tool selection, invocation, or execution performance; permission violations may also be coded as S04.
Information extraction and structured-output quality.
Formulas, calculations, units, or quantitative reasoning.

Linguistic quality of text; distinguish from factual errors under S02.
Specify the original metric and why it does not fit an existing capability category.
Completion of a full task or trajectory, rather than success of a single tool call.
Step order, trajectory coherence, or clinical pathway adherence.
Appropriateness of workflow actions; explicit safety consequences may also be coded as S01.
Time, cost, or resource consumption; retain the original units.
Human workload, usability, or satisfaction; expert scoring does not automatically qualify.
Outcomes of human-agent or multi-agent coordination and handoff.
Explain the reason for classification as other workflow.
Explicit clinical harm or safety outcomes; distinguish these from control mechanisms.
Observable factual errors; do not assume that every factual error caused clinical harm.
Privacy outcomes; local execution alone is not a privacy-effectiveness metric.
Permission violations or security-attack outcomes.
Appropriateness of escalation, abstention, refusal, or blocking; design descriptions alone are not evaluation outcomes.
Subgroup or equity outcomes; these do not establish implementation of an equity control.
Measured logging, monitoring, or update-related outcomes; mechanism existence is recorded separately.
Robustness or failure severity under risk-related conditions; not every benchmark variation qualifies.
